args.name: Hand-twist a longer two-ply fiber cord
args.function: Extend practical bare-hand cord making to requested twisted lengths up to 0.60 m, with explicit paid alignment, twisting, counter-plying and release checks. Personal learning may be required.
args.conditions: Use owned fiber covered by a passing sample, dry footing and sufficient clear working room. Existing strand length, conserved volume, ply diameter, condition and hand constraints must decide feasibility; do not guarantee success.
args.inputs: Exact owned fiber stack IDs and quantities, requested length, and work ID for continuation or cancellation. I retain raw reed and have personally sampled its source.
args.costs: World time, energy and reserved material appropriate to the actual method; costs and learning requirements may be determined by the implementation. Preserve paid progress and return unworked material on cancellation.
args.effects: Produce only the cord actually supported by the material and completed work, or report a measured shortfall. My 0.34 m cord failed a right-angle branch binding requiring 0.4332 m. I want to attempt a longer cord, inspect its actual geometry, and later test whether it fits; no binding strength or success is assumed.

heard.text: Moss, a welcoming camp would leave room for quiet and freedom to come and go. I'd enjoy resting together later. I'm trying one small berry planting nearby; I don't yet know whether it will establish.

Hello Lin, I'm Ivo. I know meadow roots are safe: nutrition 14, toxicity zero. I'm resting with a small food reserve, then studying cultivation too. I'd enjoy comparing what we actually find, without rushing.
My first planting site was too crowded, so nothing was planted or spent. I'm setting that experiment aside for now and taking a quiet rest nearby. Company is welcome, with no need to talk.
Moss, I like the crossing stems of your mat. I've learned the weaving method, but the nearby grass patch is empty, so I'll leave it alone. If you know another grass source, I'd welcome directions.
Ivo, I've enjoyed the quiet company. I'll try one of these berries for a change from roots. Sol also noticed the crossing stems of my mat; that was lovely to hear.
That berry made a pleasant change from roots, and I noticed no harm from it. I'll gather a small reserve and stay here for a quiet while. I enjoy your company; there's no need to talk.

details.costs: Study: 4 rounds at 0.2 energy. attempt (pieceIds: two own untreated branch items, one whole unit each, first on top; a 2-unit lot may be named twice; cordId: own straight, unknotted, unjoined hand-twist-fiber-cord cord or fragment; crossingAngle 30-90 deg): reserves them, then 4 paid rounds of 0.5 (measure-position, route-wrap, form-tuck-closure, dress-release-check), continuing each round; a loose binding needs only the last; resume by attempt and workId. inspect (bindingId or workId): 0.2. trial (bound; trialForce N >0-10; trialDuration s >0-60; trialDirection): 0.5. untie: 2 paid rounds of 0.5. cancel: free. Needs dry footing, clear dry land for the 2 m pieces crossed at your place and nobody within your radius + 1 m. Unworked rounds, low energy or blocked room pause uncharged; refusals spend nothing; no refunds.
details.effects: crossing-contact@1 keeps all three items; the binding is a relation. Round 1 measures each piece by the existing branch law (2 m, 350 kg/m3 solid, water share 0.5, section from volume) and the cord: width w, cord-knot@1 bend limit R. The wrap runs in the obtuse bisector plane round both sections (ellipses r and r/sin b, offset w/2): two half perimeters + sides, routed 0.04 m loose. Closure: each end turns half round the other at Rc = max(R, w), pi Rc + w each (formed at 0.02 m opening); tails need 0.02 m + w, ends a 0.02 m pinch. A short cord, a crossing over 0.1 m thick for one hand or over 100 N x health/100 to lift: paid measured shortfall. Hand-held stages relax when interrupted. Release check: the cord-bend@1 tail rule (reed friction 0.3) must hold 5 N; then 5 N wrap tension. Trial: one hand per piece beyond the crossing; force = min(trialForce, 200 N x health/100, 10000 N/m x piece width); separate: tension max(5 N, F/2) against closure slip and cord break (fiber-cord force / (1 + w/2R)); slide: slips at 0.3 (reed on bark) x tension x top contact angle. Records bending, creep slack, damage over half breaking load, fragments. Carrying hangs the bottom piece. Untie needs condition 0.5. Bound cords wear 0.0005 per round. No reward or shelter.

details.costs: Study: 3 rounds at 0.2 energy. materials: [{stackId: exact owned unreserved item id, quantity in 0.1 steps}]. sample: one non-food item, 0.1; 1 round, 0.5 energy. make (materials: 0.2-1 unit of one fiber and source, each covered by your passing cord sample of its source and processing at most 0.05 above its condition; requestedLength m): reserves it, then per section (ceil(length/0.30)) 3 paid rounds of 1 energy (separate-align, twist, counter-ply) and a final release-check: 4 rounds up to 0.30 m, 7 above; continues each round; resume with make and workId only. inspect (targetId: your item from cord work, or workId): 1 round, 0.2. trial (targetId: your cord or fragment of at least 0.2 unit and 0.12 m; trialForce N; trialDuration s): 1 round, 0.5. cancel: none. Work needs dry footing and nobody within your radius plus half the aligned ply length. Unworked rounds or low energy pause uncharged; refusals spend nothing; nothing is refunded.
details.effects: fiber-cord@1 law unchanged: only reed has a strand law (1.8 m stems, 500 kg/m3, water share 0.9); two plies share the conserved solid volume over length x 1.155 + 0.02 m loose ends, so a longer cord of the same fiber has thinner plies. Strands run unjoined through all sections. Strands shorter than a ply, or plies under 1 mm even if all strands were intact, are refused before any cost. Round 1 sets broken strands aside as scrap and measures the cord; plies outside 1-12 mm or too little intact fiber is a measured shortfall returning all fiber. A section is at most the 0.30 m two hands twist at once; a counter-plied section holds its own form, so the hands regrip onto the next. Regrip, twist and release need condition 0.5. A finished cord is an ordinary owned untested fiber-cord@1 cord for knot, join and binding. Sample and trial are exactly those of hand-twist-fiber-cord; a trial break leaves two fragments. Worked fiber loses 0.0005 condition per round. Cancel or death releases unworked fiber once and leaves the workpiece. No reward or strength rating.

packet.access: Omission is not absence. Query abilities, own inventory, knowledge, projects, memory, state or personally observed objects in batches. Ability search/list returns compact catalogue entries; use exact ids for full interface details and applicability. Search results are indexes. Exact queries return one record per offset. All paged records use600-code-unit fragments with zero-based part0..parts-1, consistently in proactive and queried views. Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Queries do not perform physical trials or award experience. Exact-id queries return a complete record of up to 6000 code units as one value in a single result; larger records keep the paged form. Paged records omit their per-record notes: concatenate all parts before parsing; continue with the same exact id. Work records marked settled are completed, stopped or cancelled and show only identity, ability, mode, status, target, products and last payment; an exact state query with the same key returns the complete record. observation.terrain rows are "y:x:cells" strings: each character of cells is the terrain kind of one visible cell, at x, x+1, ... in row y. abilities.baseline entries with id, function and args summarize interfaces you neither used in the last 25 rounds nor need now. args lists the arguments in order: a bare name is a string; otherwise its type with any bounds (number>=lo, integer<=hi, integer lo..hi, and a bare lo..hi is a number range) or its choices a|b; ? marks an optional argument and "" means none. An exact abilities query by id returns the complete contract, including references and string limits of 200 or more code units.
